subject: maths
title: Telling the Time
seo_title: Year 3 Telling the Time Worksheets: Analog and Digital Clocks to the Minute (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Describe the relationship between the hours and minutes on analog and digital clocks, and read the time to the nearest minute
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on telling the time: o’clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to, 5 minutes and the nearest minute on analog and digital clocks, am and pm, units of time and how long events last. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Australian Curriculum and useful for NAPLAN.
key_big: Short hand: the hour. Long hand: count in 5s, then on in 1s.
key_sub: 60 minutes = 1 hour. Right-hand side: minutes past. Left-hand side: minutes to the next hour, so 25 to 9 is 8:35. am is before midday, pm is after midday.
body_html:
Hours and minutes on an analog clock

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand goes all the way around once, 60 minutes pass. In that time the short hand moves from one number to the next: 60 minutes = 1 hour.

Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand, so count in 5s.

Past and to

When the long hand is on the right-hand side, say minutes past the hour. When it is on the left-hand side, say minutes to the next hour.

DigitalWe say
4:004 o’clock
4:15quarter past 4
4:2020 past 4
4:30half past 4
4:3525 to 5
4:45quarter to 5
4:5010 to 5

To the nearest minute

Between two numbers there are 5 small marks, one for each minute. Count in 5s to the last number, then on in 1s.

Read to the minute

The long hand is 3 small marks past the 4. The short hand is between 6 and 7.

Count in 5s to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. Then 21, 22, 23.

Answer: 23 minutes past 6, or 6:23

Digital clocks, am and pm

A digital clock shows the hour, then a colon, then the minutes: 4:37 means 37 minutes past 4. am is from midnight to midday (night and morning). pm is from midday to midnight (afternoon and evening).

am or pm?

Isla eats breakfast at 25 to 8. Write the time.

25 to 8 is 35 minutes past 7. Breakfast is in the morning, so it is am.

Answer: 7:35 am

Units of time

UnitEquals
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes
1 day24 hours
1 week7 days
1 fortnight14 days
1 year12 months

To compare times, change them to the same unit. 2 minutes = 120 seconds, so 2 minutes is longer than 100 seconds.

How long? Count on

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Jump to the next o’clock first, then on to the end time.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
“25 to 9” written as 9:3525 to 9 is before 9 o’clock: 60 − 25 = 35, so 8:35
Long hand on 4 read as 4 minutesEach number is 5 minutes: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes
Half past 3 read as half past 4The short hand has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is still 3
8:40 said as “20 past 8”The long hand is on the left-hand side, so it is 20 to 9
Breakfast at 7:30 pmMorning times are am: 7:30 am
10:50 to 11:20 worked out as 1120 − 1050 = 70 minutesCount on: 10 + 20 = 30 minutes

faq.q: What time should a Year 3 student be able to tell in Australia?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M3M04), Year 3 students read the time to the nearest minute on analog and digital clocks and describe how the hours and minutes are related.

faq.q: What is the difference between am and pm?
faq.a: am times are from midnight to midday (night and morning). pm times are from midday to midnight (afternoon and evening), so school starts at an am time and dinner is at a pm time.

faq.q: Is telling the time tested in NAPLAN?
faq.a: Measurement, including time, is part of the Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy test. Reading clocks and working out how long events last are useful skills to practise.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn to tell the time?
faq.a: Use a real analog clock at home and ask the time at everyday moments, such as breakfast or bedtime. Start with o’clock and half past, then quarter past and quarter to, then count in 5s and on in 1s.

sets.title: O’clock, half past, quarter past, quarter to and 5 minutes

items.e: The short hour hand points to 1. The long minute hand points to 12, so it is exactly on the hour. It is 1 o’clock. (The long hand tells the minutes, so do not read the short hand as minutes.)
The short hour hand points to 6. The long minute hand points to 12, so it is exactly on the hour. It is 6 o’clock. (The long hand tells the minutes, so do not read the short hand as minutes.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand points to 6. Count in 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes past. Half past means 30 minutes past. The hour hand has not reached 3 yet, so it is half past 2, not half past 3.

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is still 4. The long minute hand points to 6. Count in 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes past. Half past means 30 minutes past. The hour hand has not reached 5 yet, so it is half past 4, not half past 5.
The short hour hand points to 7. The long minute hand points to 12, so it is exactly on the hour. It is 7 o’clock. (The long hand tells the minutes, so do not read the short hand as minutes.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand points to 6. Count in 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes past. Half past means 30 minutes past. The hour hand has not reached 9 yet, so it is half past 8, not half past 9.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand points to 3. Count in 5s: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes past. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, and the minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past. It is quarter past 9.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand points to 3. Count in 5s: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes past. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, and the minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past. It is quarter past 12.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand points to 6. Count in 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes past. Half past means 30 minutes past. The hour hand has not reached 10 yet, so it is half past 9, not half past 10.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. The long minute hand points to 3. Count in 5s: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes past. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, and the minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past. It is quarter past 1.

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11, so the hour is still 10. The long minute hand points to 9. Count in 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes past. 45 minutes past 10 is 15 minutes before 11 o’clock. The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to the next hour: quarter to 11.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand points to 9. Count in 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes past. 45 minutes past 9 is 15 minutes before 10 o’clock. The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to the next hour: quarter to 10.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand points to 2. Count in 5s: 2 × 5 = 10 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 7. It is 10 past 7.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand points to 4. Count in 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 8. It is 20 past 8.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand points to 8. Count in 5s: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes past. That is 20 minutes before 1 o’clock (60 − 40 = 20). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 1. It is 20 to 1.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand points to 11. Count in 5s: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes past. That is 5 minutes before 8 o’clock (60 − 55 = 5). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 8. It is 5 to 8.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. The long minute hand points to 5. Count in 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 1. It is 25 past 1.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes past. That is 10 minutes before 6 o’clock (60 − 50 = 10). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 6. It is 10 to 6.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand points to 7. Count in 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past. That is 25 minutes before 10 o’clock (60 − 35 = 25). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 10. It is 25 to 10.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand points to 1. Count in 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 9. It is 5 past 9.

sets.title: Reading the time to the nearest minute

items.e: The short hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 12: 3 minutes past. So the digital time is 3:03.
The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 5. Count in 5s to 25, then on in 1s: 28 minutes past. So the digital time is 7:28.

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is still 11. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 8. Count in 5s to 40, then on in 1s: 41 minutes past. So the digital time is 11:41. (Not 12:41: the hour hand has not reached 12 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 10. Count in 5s to 50, then on in 1s: 53 minutes past. So the digital time is 6:53. (Not 7:53: the hour hand has not reached 7 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 18 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so say past: 18 minutes past 2.
The short hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 16 minutes past. So the digital time is 2:16.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 39 minutes past. So the digital time is 1:39. (Not 2:39: the hour hand has not reached 2 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 38 minutes past. That is 38 minutes past 8. It is after half past, so count the minutes to 9: 60 − 38 = 22. It is 22 minutes to 9.

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 7:48 is 48 minutes past 7. That is after half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 48 = 12 minutes to 8: 12 minutes to 8.
The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 12: 2 minutes past. So the digital time is 5:02.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 38 minutes past. That is 38 minutes past 9. It is after half past, so count the minutes to 10: 60 − 38 = 22. It is 22 minutes to 10.

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is still 4. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 48 minutes past. So the digital time is 4:48. (Not 5:48: the hour hand has not reached 5 yet.)

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 2:13 is 13 minutes after 2 o’clock. It is before half past, so say past: 13 minutes past 2.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 6. Count in 5s to 30, then on in 1s: 32 minutes past. So the digital time is 7:32. (Not 8:32: the hour hand has not reached 8 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 18 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so say past: 18 minutes past 7.

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 10:51 is 51 minutes past 10. That is after half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 51 = 9 minutes to 11: 9 minutes to 11.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 10. Count in 5s to 50, then on in 1s: 53 minutes past. So the digital time is 8:53. (Not 9:53: the hour hand has not reached 9 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 8. Count in 5s to 40, then on in 1s: 41 minutes past. That is 41 minutes past 9. It is after half past, so count the minutes to 10: 60 − 41 = 19. It is 19 minutes to 10.

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 5:37 is 37 minutes past 5. That is after half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 37 = 23 minutes to 6: 23 minutes to 6.

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 21 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so say past: 21 minutes past 2.

sets.title: Analog and digital clocks with am and pm

items.e: am times go from midnight to midday (night and morning). pm times go from midday to midnight (afternoon and evening).

c: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day
items.e: Midnight is 12 o’clock at night, when one day ends and the next day starts. 12 o’clock in the middle of the day is midday (also called noon).
The afternoon is after midday, so it is a pm time. 2:30 am is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 2:30 pm.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an am time. 3:50 am is the middle of the night. So the answer is 8:50 am.

items.q: The long minute hand goes all the way around the clock once. How much time has passed?
items.e: The minute hand passes all 60 small marks, one for each minute. 60 minutes = 1 hour. In that time the short hour hand moves from one number to the next.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 2. Count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s: 14 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 6:14 pm.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 38 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 8:38 am.

items.q: Write quarter to 9 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 9” means 15 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 45 minutes past 8: 8:45. It is in the morning, so it is am: 8:45 am. (Not 9:45 am: that is after 9 o’clock.)

At 3:37 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 7 (count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s to 37), and the short hand is between 3 and 4. That is clock D. (Clock A shows 4:37; clock B shows 3:23; clock C shows 3:07.)

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 2. Count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s: 12 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 1:12 pm.

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 3: 3:35. It is in the afternoon, so it is pm: 3:35 pm. (Not 4:35 pm: that is after 4 o’clock.)

At 10:12 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 2 (count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s to 12), and the short hand is between 10 and 11. That is clock B. (Clock A shows 11:12; clock C shows 10:48; clock D shows 10:02.)

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 21 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 3:21 pm.

items.q: A digital clock shows 4:37. How many minutes is it until 5 o’clock?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. It is 37 minutes past 4. 60 − 37 = 23 minutes to 5 o’clock. (Not 63: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Write 20 past 7 in the evening as a digital time.
items.e: “20 past 7” means 20 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:20. It is in the evening, so it is pm: 7:20 pm.

At 6:52 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 10 (count in 5s to 50, then on in 1s to 52), and the short hand is between 6 and 7. That is clock C. (Clock A shows 7:52; clock B shows 6:08; clock D shows 6:10.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 47 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 7:47 pm.

items.q: Write 10 to 8 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “10 to 8” means 10 minutes before 8 o’clock. 60 − 10 = 50, so it is 50 minutes past 7: 7:50. It is in the morning, so it is am: 7:50 am. (Not 8:50 am: that is after 8 o’clock.)

At 7:26 the long hand is 1 small mark past the 5 (count in 5s to 25, then on in 1s to 26), and the short hand is between 7 and 8. That is clock A. (Clock B shows 8:26; clock C shows 7:34; clock D shows 7:05.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 2. Count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s: 13 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 7:13 am.

sets.title: Units of time: seconds, minutes, hours and days

items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute.
There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
There are 24 hours in 1 day: 12 am hours and 12 pm hours. 12 + 12 = 24.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days. (5 is just the school days.)

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30 minutes. (Not 50: an hour is not 100 minutes.)

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. (25 would be a quarter of 100.)

items.q: A fortnight is 2 weeks. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 2 weeks = 7 + 7 = 14 days. (10 is only the school days in 2 weeks.)
January to December: 12 months. (52 is the number of weeks.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 2 minutes = 60 + 60 = 120 seconds.
1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 hours = 60 + 60 = 120 minutes. (Not 200: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 30 = 90 seconds. (Not 130: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)
1 day = 24 hours. 2 days = 24 + 24 = 48 hours.

items.q: About how long does it take to brush your teeth?
items.e: 2 seconds is far too quick, and 2 hours is far too long. Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes.

items.q: About how long does a Year 3 student sleep at night?
items.e: Children sleep from the evening until the morning. That is about 10 hours.

items.q: Which unit would you use to time a 50 m race at the athletics carnival?
items.e: A 50 m race is over very quickly, in less than a minute. We time it in seconds.

items.q: About how long is a school day?
items.e: School starts in the morning and finishes in the afternoon. That is about 6 hours.
1 minute = 60 seconds. 50 seconds is less than 60 seconds, 70 seconds and 1 hour. So 50 seconds is the shortest.

items.q: Which is longer: 100 seconds or 2 minutes?
items.e: 2 minutes = 60 + 60 = 120 seconds. 120 seconds is more than 100 seconds, so 2 minutes is longer. (100 seconds is 1 minute 40 seconds.)

items.q: Which is longer: 1 hour or 70 minutes?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 70 minutes is 10 minutes more than 60 minutes, so 70 minutes is longer.

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: 1 hour, 1 second, 1 day, 1 minute.
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 day = 24 hours. So the order is 1 second, 1 minute, 1 hour, 1 day.

sets.title: How long? Time in daily life

items.q: A TV program starts at 4:10 pm and ends at 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Chloe starts reading at 7:05 pm and stops at 7:45 pm. How long does she read for?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.

items.q: Assembly starts at 9:05 am and ends at 9:27 am. How long is assembly?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 27 − 5 = 22 minutes.

items.q: Harper’s netball game starts at 9:15 am and ends at 9:50 am. How long is the game?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 50 − 15 = 35 minutes.

items.q: Aarav gets on the school bus at 8:20 am. He gets to school at 8:43 am. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 43 − 20 = 23 minutes.

items.q: Recess starts at 10:50 am and ends at 11:20 am. How long is recess?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 10:50 am to 11:00 am is 10 minutes. Then 11:00 am to 11:20 am is 20 minutes. 10 + 20 = 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Lunch starts at 12:50 pm and ends at 1:30 pm. How long is lunch?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 12:50 pm to 1:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 1:00 pm to 1:30 pm is 30 minutes. 10 + 30 = 40 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A TV program starts at 6:15 pm. It lasts 25 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 25 minutes from 6:15: 15 + 25 = 40. It is still the evening, so it ends at 6:40 pm.

items.q: At the school sausage sizzle, the sausages go on the barbecue at 11:48 am. They come off at 12:03 pm. How long do they cook?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes. Then 12:00 pm to 12:03 pm is 3 minutes. 12 + 3 = 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Ethan’s swimming lesson is from 3:50 pm to 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:50 pm to 4:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 4:00 pm to 4:35 pm is 35 minutes. 10 + 35 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Sport starts at 1:40 pm. It lasts 50 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: From 1:40 pm, 20 minutes takes you to 2:00 pm. 50 − 20 = 30 more minutes makes 2:30 pm. (2:40 pm would be 1 hour later, not 50 minutes.)

items.q: Mia goes to bed at 7:30 pm. She has a shower 20 minutes before bed. What time does the shower start?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes from 7:30: 30 − 20 = 10. The shower starts at 7:10 pm. (7:50 pm is 20 minutes after bedtime.)

items.q: School starts at 8:50 am. Recess starts at 10:50 am. How long is it from the start of school to recess?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 8:50 am to 9:00 am is 10 minutes. Then 9:00 am to 10:50 am is 1 hour 50 minutes. 10 + 110 = 120 minutes = 2 hours. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: The bus for the school excursion leaves at 9:20 am. The trip takes 1 hour 25 minutes. What time does the bus arrive?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 9:20 am → 10:20 am. Then add 25 minutes: 20 + 25 = 45. The bus arrives at 10:45 am.

items.q: A footy match starts at 1:45 pm and ends at 3:50 pm. How long is the match?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 1:45 pm to 2:00 pm is 15 minutes. Then 2:00 pm to 3:50 pm is 1 hour 50 minutes. 15 + 110 = 125 minutes = 2 hours 5 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: School starts at 8:50 am and finishes at 3:10 pm. How long is the school day?
items.e: 8:50 am to 2:50 pm is 6 hours. 2:50 pm to 3:10 pm is 20 minutes. So the school day is 6 hours 20 minutes.

items.q: Kai’s movie lasts 1 hour 30 minutes. Grace’s movie lasts 95 minutes. Whose movie is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 30 minutes = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes. 95 − 90 = 5. So Grace’s movie is longer, by 5 minutes.

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Ava runs a race in 58 seconds. Ruby takes 1 minute 5 seconds. How much faster is Ava?
items.e: 1 minute 5 seconds = 60 + 5 = 65 seconds. 65 − 58 = 7 seconds. (Not 47: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)

items.q: Mei practises reading for 15 minutes a day for 4 days. How long is that in total?
items.e: 4 × 15 = 60 minutes. 60 minutes = 1 hour.

items.q: The school holidays last 2 weeks and 3 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 2 weeks = 14 days. 14 + 3 = 17 days. (23 days would mean a week of 10 days.)
